subject: Civil Engineering
title: Cost Estimating
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cost Estimating.

hook.text: How much will this building cost? The estimate determines whether it gets built at all.

buildup.text: Conceptual estimates use cost per square foot — rough but fast during early planning.

discovery.text: Detailed estimates price every material, labor hour, and equipment rental — the definitive number.

twist.text: Contingency — 5-15% added for unknowns — is always included. The unknown always happens.

climax.text: The Sydney Opera House was estimated at $7 million. It cost $102 million — a 14x overrun.

punchline.text: An estimate is a guess with math behind it. Better math makes better guesses.

quiz.question: Why is contingency always included in construction cost estimates?
options: To cover the contractor's profit margin
To account for unknowns and uncertainties that inevitably arise during construction
To pay for design changes requested by the architect

details.summary: Construction cost estimating predicts the total cost of a project by quantifying materials, labor, equipment, subcontractors, overhead, and profit for every work item.
details.whyItMatters: Accurate cost estimates are the foundation of project budgets, financing decisions, and bid evaluations. Systematic underestimation is the leading cause of project cost overruns worldwide.
takeaways: Conceptual estimates use cost per square meter from similar completed projects
Detailed estimates quantify every material, labor hour, and equipment item
Contingency allowances account for unforeseen conditions and design gaps

faq.question: Why do construction projects so often exceed their initial cost estimates?
faq.answer: Common causes include optimistic estimating to secure project approval, incomplete design at the time of estimating, unforeseen site conditions, scope changes during construction, material price escalation, and inadequate contingency allowances.

faq.question: What is a quantity takeoff in construction estimating?
faq.answer: A quantity takeoff is the systematic measurement of all materials and work items from construction drawings and specifications. Estimators measure areas, volumes, lengths, and counts for every element: cubic meters of concrete, tons of steel, square meters of formwork, meters of pipe, and so on.
